newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai cabinet approves confidence measures.
newsitem.headline: Thai cabinet approves confidence measures.

text.p: The Thai cabinet on Tuesday approved a series of measures aimed at bolstering confidence in the beleaguered finance sector, a government statement said.
Most of the measures have already been announced by authorities over the past few days.
One is a plan to set up a deposit insurance institution within one year in an effort to boost depositors' confidence.
The Bank of Thailand on Monday announced a series of measures to allay depositor fears about their money after authorities launched a massive shake-up of the finance sector.
Thai authorities on Friday forced 16 ailing finance firms to come up with plans to merge or have their licences revoked and be absorbed by healthy firms under purchase and assumption arrangements.
They suspended the operations of the 16 troubled firms for 30 days and gave them two weeks to come up with concrete plans for their future.
The cabinet on Tuesday also approved a finance ministry plan to waive capital gains taxes on gains which occur from the mergers, the statement said.
It also approved a cap on deposit rates announced on Monday, which is aimed at helping to ease the interest burden for financial institutions.
Under the plan, commercial bank deposit rates were limited at 12 percent, finance firm promissory note rates at 14 percent and finance firms' call rates at 11 percent.
